mechanism_narrative: A persistently low federal funds rate (below 0.5%) compresses the discount rate for equity valuations, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days. This signal is active whenever the rate is below the threshold, but the mechanism is always-on in the sense that the rate level is continuously monitored.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of instances when FEDFUNDS is below 0.5%, or the Rank IC over a 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the unemployment rate above 5.5% indicates deteriorating labor market conditions, reducing consumer spending and corporate earnings, which leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 40% of instances when UNRATE > 5.5%, or the Rank IC over a 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A combination of strong labor market growth (PAYEMS) and weak industrial production (INDPRO) indicates an economy with rising wage pressures and supply constraints, prompting central bank tightening and negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 50% of instances when PAYEMS is above 140,000 and INDPRO is below 100, or the Rank IC over a 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: During a monetary tightening cycle (defined by FEDFUNDS above 1.0%), the S&P 500 experiences negative returns over the next 60 days due to reduced liquidity and higher borrowing costs.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive in more than 40% of instances when FEDFUNDS > 1.0%, or the Rank IC over a 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: Higher housing starts (HOUST) indicate robust consumer demand and economic expansion, which boosts corporate earnings and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are negative in more than 50% of instances when HOUST is above 1000, or the Rank IC over a 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in retail sales (RSAFS) below 440,000 million dollars signals weak consumer spending, reducing corporate revenue expectations and causing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 40% of instances when RSAFS < 440000, or the Rank IC over a 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: Strong GDP growth (GDPC1) combined with weak industrial production (INDPRO) signals an overheating economy with supply constraints, prompting central bank intervention and negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive in more than 50% of instances when GDPC1 is above 16000 and INDPRO is below 100, or the Rank IC over a 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: During a labor market recovery (defined by UNRATE falling below 5.0% and PAYEMS rising above 140,000 thousand), the S&P 500 experiences positive returns over the next 20 days due to improving corporate earnings and consumer confidence.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 50% of instances when UNRATE < 5.0% and PAYEMS > 140000, or the Rank IC over a 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.
